claims.text: A simulation explicitly incorporating mass variation, force-constant variation, local lattice distortion, and anharmonicity will accurately predict lattice thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice and electronic heat transport can be treated as separate channels in the proposed simulation.
The proposed approach will reduce lattice-conductivity prediction error by approximately 20–30% relative to prior Debye- and DFT-based approximations over 300–1200 K.
The proposed approach will produce trends consistent with measurements below 200 K and between 300 and 1200 K.
The modeled initial state is a defect-free bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystal.
Most previous simulations of the material assumed defect-free bulk-crystal configurations.
A combined DFT/molecular-dynamics or similar technique can fully account for atomic-scale disorder and independently calculate phononic transport.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
The predictions are intended to apply up to 1200 K and to samples containing as much as 1 wt.% oxygen.
Mass variation, force-constant variation, and local lattice distortion govern phonon-scattering mechanisms that determine lattice thermal conductivity.
Separating phononic and electronic transport enables better treatment of anharmonic interactions and scattering in disordered HfNbTaTiZr.
Avoiding reliance on a Debye temperature yields a more accurate temperature dependence for lattice thermal conductivity.
Earlier approaches conflated or inadequately separated lattice and electronic contributions.
The approximations in earlier approaches caused poorer quantitative agreement with experiments.
The model will be less accurate for samples containing more than 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model may be less accurate when electron–phonon coupling is non-negligible.
Magnetic-field dependence or specific-heat measurements can be used as complementary techniques to separate the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution.
Deviation of measured lattice thermal conductivity from predictions by more than ±30%, or failure to reproduce the predicted temperature dependence, is stipulated to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as defect-free, while the claimed applicability includes specimens with up to 1 wt.% oxygen. Oxygen at that concentration is an extrinsic compositional impurity, so the sample scope is not consistently defined as defect-free.
